Lockheed Martin and the Pentagon have reached a preliminary 10-year agreement to produce at least 850 F-35 fighter jets.
Lockheed will invest at least $7 billion of its own funds to support production, targeting 156 jets annually. 
The deal also covers international orders and aims to reduce costs and supply-chain bottlenecks.
The agreement is not yet a firm order, and its execution remains subject to congressional approval and funding.
